ps140: Today, Your precious Cross* has shone forth radiantly like the sun, O Saviour Christ,* set up and elevated on the all-glorious place of the skull, on Your all-holy mountain,* showing forth most manifestly that it is thereby, O Omnipotent One,* that You have raised our nature up to the heavens,* in that You love mankind.

Today, O Unapproachable One,* the heavens have declared Your glory to men;* for the image of the Cross, shining forth in radiance with unapproachable light,* has denounced the savage and cruel nature of those who slew God.* Therefore, we glorify Your loving dispensation, O almighty Jesus,* Saviour of our souls.

By stretching forth his arms Moses vanquished Amalek,* prefiguring the image of the Cross;* and we now, bowing down before the tree of the Cross,* trample the wiles and machinations of the enemy underfoot,* having Christ as our champion,* who was lifted up upon it in the flesh,* slew the serpent and saved man.

You did not fear the wrath of the wretched and Christ-hating king,* O most wise Michael;* you were not weakened by the will to live or by the desire for the princedom which you left of your own accord.* Instead, you confessed Christ to be the only God, saying:* “Him alone I worship from my soul,* and it is sweet for me to die for Him Who died for me!“* Pray to Him, O passion-bearer Michael with your nobleman Theodore,* to save all who honour you.

“Spare your youth“, says the torturer,* “and prostrate yourself before the god whom I desire* —the sun and the fire—* and reign with me!“* But you, O martyr, answered: “May it never be for me, O most iniquitous one,* to renounce Christ, and to bow down to your false gods!* What is the suffering that you threaten me with,* or even this life,* compared to the Kingdom to come?“* Therefore, O most wise Michael,* pray with your nobleman Theodore* that we, who always honour you with love,* may also obtain that Kingdom.

The king, wretched and utterly estranged from God,* attempted to turn you away from the faith in Christ, O Michael, by deceit,* striving to persuade you with pleasing words.* For he said “If you bow to my god I desire,* you will enjoy the glory of this world with me!“* But the wicked man sinned in his hope and was ensnared in the work of his own hands.* By the prayers of your servants, O Christ,* deliver us from such inhumanity,* for You alone are gracious and love mankind.

O passion-bearer, you said:* “You promise to give me the riches of this world and a perishing kingdom,* but you yourself will leave it against your will!* I will in no way renounce Christ,* but confess Him alone to be the Creator of heaven and earth,* and I trust Him without doubt.“* Therefore pray to Him, O glory of martyrs Michael, together with your good nobleman Theodore,* that we who honour you with love may be saved.

By crossing his hands in the blessing of his children,* the Patriarch Jacob foreshadowed the powerful sign of the Cross.* We now have it as our safeguard that cannot be overthrown,* and with its strength we drive out the hosts of demons.* Casting down the arrogance of Belial with it,* we put to flight the destroying power of Amalek.* And now that it is lifted on high,* we the faithful offer it in devotion* for the cleansing of our sins before the goodness of God.* We cry aloud with the fullness of our voices:* Have mercy on us, O Lord made flesh of a Virgin;* take pity on us, O Gracious One,* for we are the works which you fashioned in Your wisdom.
aposticha: Like, a bride is the Church splendidly adorned with the water of grace* and Your Blood, O Word,* singing the glory of the Cross.
Raising aloft the spear and the Cross,* the nails and all else by which the life-bearing body of Christ was pierced,* let us worship them.
When Moses conquered Amalek, keeping his arms raised aloft,* he prefigured the all-pure suffering of Christ* in the form of the Cross.

O saints, adorned with the beauty of your deeds* and clothed in the garment of your blood,* you were proven to be bright luminaries for the world by the grace of the Spirit,* enlightening your native land, O pious and noble scions,* passion-bearer and confessor of Christ Michael* together with Theodore.* Standing with the martyrs before the face of the Lord,* pray for salvation of our souls,* as we honour your memory with piety and love.

Cross of Christ, hope of Christians,* guide for the lost,* haven of the storm-tossed, victory in battles,* strength and confirmation for the world,* physician of the sick, Resurrection of the dead:* Have mercy on us!
